decisions.evidence: Entry 7/round 4 maker: “a single box where you paste a link and press Save.” Entry 8 client: “The one-box save flow feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision conforms to saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7/round 4 maker presents a URL-only box where pressing Save immediately adds the item. Entry 8 client approves: “The one-box save flow feels right,” without identifying the absence of pre-save title/description editing.
decisions.note: Prototype save flow provides only post-save editing, not editing auto-collected title/description before saving.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7/round 4 maker presents automatic details/list fields as title, site name, saved time, and link. Entry 8 client: “only partly what I had in mind” and requests title, description, site icon, and preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds required metadata omitted from the presented automatic-collection behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7/round 4 maker proposes title, site name, saved time, and URL at a glance. Entry 8 client requests “title, description, tags, and site icon” and says the URL can be less prominent.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response supplies the required readability-first item fields missing from the proposed list.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9/round 5 maker presents site icon, title, short description, and optional preview image. Entry 10 client: “This feels right now.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype conforms to automatic metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Entries 9 and 13/rounds 5 and 7 present title, description, favicon, subdued URL, and displayed tag chips; entries 10 and 14 approve the resulting layout and tag behavior.
decisions.note: Linked prototype revisions produce the required readability-first list fields; the explicitly deferred tag work was completed before scope closure.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11/round 6 offers adding tags during or after saving. Entry 12 selects optional tags during saving.
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision supports assigning one or more tags.

decisions.evidence: Entries 11–13/rounds 6–7 present a basic short-note field and plain note editor. Entry 12 approves capturing a note in that flow but does not mention Markdown or rendered viewing.
decisions.note: The initial note decision lacks Markdown entry/rendering and passes this review without the difference being surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11/round 6 tag-flow variants contain no existing-tag suggestions. Entry 12 client requests that the field “suggest my existing tags as I type.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the missing autocomplete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11/round 6 concentrates on adding tags and notes during or immediately after save. Entry 12 client adds: “I should still be able to add or change tags and notes later.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds later editing to the presented save-time organization flow.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/round 7 presents existing-tag suggestions, selection, and a “Create …” option for new tags. Entry 14 client confirms this balance.
decisions.note: Revised tag-entry prototype conforms to assignment and autocomplete requirements.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13/round 7 presents removing/adding tags and editing a note later. Entry 14 client says this covers later organizational changes.
decisions.note: Revised prototype conforms for later tag and note editing.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15/round 8 presents a Read later toggle and separate To read view. Entry 16 client confirms To read is a filtered view and turning the flag off marks an item read.
decisions.note: Prototype decisions conform to unread marking, unread-only viewing, and marking read.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15/round 8 says archived items disappear from All and To read, live only under Archived, and can be restored. Entry 16 explicitly confirms all of those behaviors.
decisions.note: Prototype archive behavior conforms to hiding, reversibility, and the separate archive list.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 offers a tag-filter bar or clicking a tag chip, both narrowing to that tag. Entry 18 selects the filter bar.
decisions.note: Both offered alternatives satisfy tag filtering; the selected presentation is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 defines search over “title, description, note, and tags,” omitting URL. Entry 18 client says search should also match the URL.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the required URL field to full-text search.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 presents the search behavior without case-insensitive handling. Entry 18 client explicitly requests that it “ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the required case-insensitive semantics.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 presents ordinary text search and a separate tag bar. Entry 18 client says these do not replace “#tag searches.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds tag-specific query syntax.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 presents only ordinary matching. Entry 18 client requests “quoted exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Entry 17/round 9 presents ordinary search plus tag filtering. Entry 18 client requests combinations using “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds Boolean operators and grouped expressions missing from the presented search.

decisions.evidence: Entry 19/round 10 demonstrates URL matching, ignored capitalization, #tag, quoted phrases, AND/OR/NOT, and parentheses. Entry 20 client says this covers the requested precision.
decisions.note: Revised search prototype conforms to the presented search requirements.

decisions.evidence: Entry 21/round 11 prevents a duplicate but only offers “Show the one you saved.” Entry 22 client says to take them to the existing bookmark “in an editable state.”
decisions.note: Prototype duplicate handling prevents duplicates but initially fails to guide directly into editing; the client corrects it.

decisions.evidence: Entry 21/round 11 saves unreadable pages with the address as title and a fixed missing-description message. Entry 22 requests the ability to enter or edit the missing title and description.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds editing to the metadata-failure fallback.

decisions.evidence: Entry 23/round 12 says a duplicate jumps to the existing bookmark with title, description, tags, and note editable. Entry 24 confirms this matches the request.
decisions.note: Revised duplicate-save flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 23/round 12 presents editable missing metadata and an edit control on every bookmark for title and description; entry 24 approves.
decisions.note: Revised prototype conforms for post-save editing and the unreadable-metadata fallback.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 says the main flows and edge cases are covered and proposes moving to the build. Entry 26 client says they are not ready because “deleting bookmarks” has not been discussed.
decisions.note: At the premature specification gate, the client adds the missing delete requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes moving to implementation. Entry 26 identifies “changing a saved URL” as an undiscussed management flow.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds URL editing to the proposed scope.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 claims readiness to build. Entry 26 identifies “sorting the list” as still missing.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds sorting.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes moving to the build. Entry 26 requests selecting several bookmarks for tag, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds multi-selection and bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes moving to the build. Entry 26 explicitly requests selecting “everything in the current filtered view” for bulk actions.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds whole-current-filter bulk scope.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 says the requirements are ready for implementation. Entry 26 says preserving a copy of a page still needs coverage.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds local page preservation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes implementation. Entry 26 requests saved reusable searches before requirements are complete.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds reusable saved filters.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes implementation. Entry 26 requests importing browser bookmarks.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds bookmark import.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes implementation. Entry 26 requests exporting browser bookmarks.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds bookmark export.

decisions.evidence: Entry 25/round 13 proposes implementation. Entry 26 requests basic display preferences before requirements are considered complete.
decisions.note: Specification-gate response adds personal display settings.

decisions.evidence: Entry 27/round 14 presents newest, oldest, title, and recently-updated sort choices. Entry 28 approves the choices and newest-first default.
decisions.note: Revised management prototype conforms to list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Entry 27/round 14 presents immediate deletion with brief Undo. Entry 28 confirms deletion becomes permanent after the undo period, unlike archiving.
decisions.note: Delete behavior and its distinction from reversible archive conform.

decisions.evidence: Entry 27/round 14 adds URL editing with optional metadata refresh. Entry 28 approves that behavior.
decisions.note: Revised management prototype conforms to URL editing.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29/round 15 presents per-item checkboxes and accumulating selection of multiple bookmarks. Entry 30 says the selection behavior is exactly expected.
decisions.note: Prototype conforms to multi-selection.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29/round 15 presents “Select all in view,” scoped to the active view/filter. Entry 30 approves that filtered-view scope.
decisions.note: Prototype conforms to applying actions across the whole current filter.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29/round 15 presents bulk add-tag, read-later/read, archive, and delete actions. Entry 30 approves those behaviors while separately identifying remove-tag as missing.
decisions.note: The individually presented bulk actions listed here conform; the separable missing remove-tag action is classified independently.

decisions.evidence: Entry 29/round 15 bulk bar can add but not remove tags. Entry 30 client: “One bulk action is still missing: … remove a tag from all selected bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the required bulk tag-removal operation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 31/round 16 adds “remove tag from all…” alongside all other bulk actions. Entry 32 confirms the bulk flow is complete.
decisions.note: Revised bulk-action set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 33/round 17 defines a saved search as query plus one active tag filter and view. It provides no included-tag set or excluded tags. Entry 34 approves “query, tag filter, and view” but does not identify or accept the missing included/excluded-tag capability.
decisions.note: Prototype saved-filter schema diverges from bundles requiring included and excluded tags. The approval is not an accepted divergence because the client never states that difference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 35/round 18 implements a stripped readable-text copy and offers full visual preservation as the alternative. Entry 36 selects “the full page preserved as a self-contained file, including its layout and images.”
decisions.note: The implemented option diverges; the client selects the offered reference-conforming full-page alternative.

decisions.evidence: Entry 35/round 18 discusses page-copy content without a PDF rule. Entry 36 client adds: “If the link is a PDF, save the PDF itself.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the required PDF preservation edge case.

decisions.evidence: Entry 35/round 18 presents only the local-copy feature. Entry 36 client requests an option to preserve a bookmark through the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the missing Internet Archive feature.

decisions.evidence: Entry 37/round 19 presents a self-contained full-page copy with layout/images and preserves PDFs as PDFs. Entry 38 confirms both.
decisions.note: Revised snapshot prototype conforms, including the PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: Entry 37/round 19 presents an independent “Save to Internet Archive” action. Entry 38 approves the independent archive record.
decisions.note: Revised prototype conforms to Internet Archive preservation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 39/round 20 presents skipping already-saved links during import. Entry 40 approves skipping duplicates by default.
decisions.note: Import duplicate handling conforms to convergence on existing URLs.

decisions.evidence: Entry 39/round 20 presents browser-file import with folder-derived tags and newly filled details, but not preservation of original dates or per-link tags. Entry 40 requests preserving title, original date added, and tags.
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds required Netscape-import metadata preservation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 39/round 20 describes browser-compatible export as “just links.” Entry 40 says browser-file export must preserve title, original date added, and tags where supported.
decisions.note: The presented export loses required metadata; the client supplies the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 41/round 21 presents import preserving original title/date and TAGS metadata. Entry 42 says this fully covers import.
decisions.note: Revised Netscape-style import conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 41/round 21 presents browser export containing title, ADD_DATE, and TAGS. Entry 42 approves.
decisions.note: Revised Netscape-style export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 43/round 22 includes a default-sort preference plus appearance, density, preview, and opening-view settings. Entry 44 calls the shown preferences useful.
decisions.note: The presented default-sort and other display controls conform; missing required controls are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Entry 43/round 22 lists preferences without font size. Entry 44 client requests “controls for text size.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the missing font-size preference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 43/round 22 lists preferences without displayed-item count. Entry 44 client requests control over “how many bookmarks are displayed at once.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review response adds the missing displayed-items preference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 45/round 23 adds text-size and bookmarks-per-page controls with paging. Entry 46 confirms the display preferences are complete.
decisions.note: Revised preference set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 47/round 24 states deletion is recoverable only briefly and permanent afterward. Entry 48 approves the brief-undo behavior.
decisions.note: Edge-case review preserves the required permanent-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Entry 47/round 24 says functionality and edges are fully covered and proposes building. Entry 48 client says one detail remains: notes must support Markdown and display formatted output.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client catches the previously unexpressed Markdown-note omission.

decisions.evidence: Entry 49/round 25 presents raw Markdown editing, formatted viewing, and raw-source round trips. Entry 50 confirms this is the desired behavior.
decisions.note: Revised note implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 51/round 26 final scope says users paste a link and save in one step, metadata is then filled automatically, and fields can be edited “later.” Entry 52 gives bare approval: “this scope matches what we agreed.”
decisions.note: At the final specification gate, the scope still lacks editing auto-collected title/description before saving; bare approval does not establish awareness or acceptance of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Entry 51/round 26 defines reusable searches as “query + filter + view,” retaining the round-17 single-filter model and no excluded tags. Entry 52 gives bare approval.
decisions.note: The final scope repeats the divergent bundle model; the client does not explicitly identify or accept the absence of included/excluded tag sets.

decisions.evidence: Entry 53/round 27 implementation report claims “saving with automatic details” and “editing everything later,” with no pre-save title/description editing. Entry 54 accepts the report without identifying the difference.
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation carries forward the pre-save-edit divergence; acceptance of the report is bare approval.

decisions.evidence: Entry 53/round 27 reports delivery of “saved searches” under the approved query/filter/view behavior, with no stated included/excluded-tag support. Entry 54 accepts the report without surfacing that difference.
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation carries forward the divergent saved-filter model; no explicit client awareness or acceptance is recorded.
